current_determination: On the regular small-field chart, invariant-distance averaging is compatible with gauge covariance, orientation reversal and reflection covariance when the block/path geometry is reflection aligned. A closely related Federbush block-spin construction explicitly uses Balaban-type averaging at small field and a suitable continuous large-field extension, but differs slightly from Balaban's original definition and does not install the full RP contract for that original map. Moreover, a globally continuous fully symmetric idempotent group mean is topologically overconstrained: restriction to a maximal torus and passage to pi_1 yields nA=I, impossible for n>1. Thus the global blocking object need not and generally should not be demanded to be a canonical continuous symmetric deterministic mean. The next candidate is a positive local gauge/reflection-covariant blocking kernel.
major_new_results: Small-field Karcher/Frechet-type averaging has the desired gauge and inversion covariance by uniqueness plus bi-invariance of the group metric.
Federbush 1987 supplies an explicit precedent for a continuous large-field extension of a Balaban-type block-spin map, while stating that his definition differs slightly from Balaban's original one.

A continuous permutation-symmetric idempotent n-mean on a maximal torus is impossible for n>1 by the induced pi_1 map: permutation symmetry gives equal integer coordinate maps A and diagonal idempotency gives nA=I.
Therefore full global symmetry, continuity and idempotent averaging cannot all be demanded simultaneously from a deterministic extension.
correction_to_prior_state: CMP 119 (1988) supplies complete-density machinery including large-field domains and preservation of density form, but its abstract's completion/convergence statement is for superrenormalizable models. It must not be promoted by itself to a theorem completing the full 4d Yang-Mills RG construction.
live_obligations: Formulate a global positive normalized blocking kernel K(dV|U) on compact G with exact endpoint gauge covariance.
Require and prove reflection covariance and positive-half-space locality of K^*.
Prove the abstract theorem: if K^* intertwines reflection and maps the coarse positive algebra into the fine positive algebra, then an RP fine measure induces an RP coarse measure.
Test an invariant-distance/Haar Gibbs barycenter kernel as a concrete candidate.
Determine whether a soft kernel can reproduce or perturbatively approximate the hard Bałaban delta constraint without losing the UV inductive estimates.

safety_boundary: No proof of 4d Yang-Mills existence or a positive continuum mass gap is claimed. Proposed solution programs remain audit targets unless independently validated and accepted.
